name: Retention

subjectOf.text: The retention uplifts claimed for LER remain unvalidated: empirical pilots are needed to confirm them and to refine the smart contract designs, particularly for AI-personalized airdrops.
subjectOf.abstract: Empirical pilots are needed to validate retention uplifts and refine smart contract designs.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Liquid Equity Rewards (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5454054
scope_conditions: current state of evidence as of 2025

subjectOf.text: Reward accrual scales with holding duration, for example thirty to ninety day windows, which encourages prolonged ownership in the same way DeFi liquid staking yields encourage retention, but without locking up the shareholder's ability to sell.
subjectOf.abstract: Similar to how DeFi liquid staking leverages yields to encourage retention, these payments increase over time based on holding durations (for example, 30–90 days), encouraging prolonged ownership without locking up liquidity.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Liquid Equity Rewards in Corporate America (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5583610
scope_conditions: rewards keyed to verified holding periods

subjectOf.text: LER's central comparative advantage is a projected fifteen to thirty percent reduction in shareholder turnover, benchmarked against established loyalty programs, which stabilizes the ownership base during activist-driven price swings.
subjectOf.abstract: LER's true comparative advantage lies in its ability to curb shareholder turnover by 15–30%, benchmarked against proven loyalty initiatives, which in turn helps solidify ownership amid activist-fueled swings.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Liquid Equity Rewards in Corporate America (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5583610
scope_conditions: benchmarked against loyalty share and stock option retention studies, not against LER itself

subjectOf.text: A filter that claims to address collapse must beat real-data retention, not only unfiltered replacement, because retaining ten percent of the original data slows the damage.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: The comparator standard follows from published results on real-data retention.
It sets a requirement on what a filter must show, not a result about any filter.

subjectOf.text: The frozen pass rule requires, on the five-run means from generation 0 to 9, a full-replacement perplexity rise of at least 4.0 with a margin of at least 2.0 over the rise under ten percent retention, with the thresholds sitting at fractions of the reported change so the rule does not depend on which published baseline was meant, and a miss blocks reading anything else.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: The rule governs the replication substrate, which the filter never enters.
A miss blocks every other reading, including the sealed Gaussian outcomes.

subjectOf.text: A positive reading on substrate G needs nine superior labels, and if the ten percent arm's retention exceeds 0.90 in a family the pool cannot be labeled superior to it there and no positive reading is possible.

scope_conditions: The power calculation assumes a normal approximation and a planning alternative fixed before the runs.
The stated power covers the labels only and not the gates.

subjectOf.text: The design names a failure pattern in advance: if the likelihood filter, the equal-weight pool, and the reputation pool each carry the negative label against full replacement in every family, the paper issues a registered sentence recording that each had lower capped retention at generation 50 than full replacement, as a registered negative result and not an implementation failure.
